title: Redwood Console — Left rail reframe, contextual routing & fast workspace jumps
creator: Eleanor Park
description:
Problem: The current Console navigation mixes global routes (billing, account-level settings) with workspace-scoped routes (apps, models, rollouts, dashboards) and provides no consistent location for quick workspace switching. This leads to confusion for platform users who manage multiple workspaces and makes it hard to surface important operational pages (rollouts, cost views, SLO dashboard) at glance.

Goal: Deliver an information architecture and left-rail redesign that: (1) clearly separates global vs workspace-scoped entry points, (2) surfaces high-value operational pages (dashboards, rollouts, cost breakdowns) with reduced click depth, (3) introduces a fast, keyboard-first workspace switcher and compact workspace context pill, and (4) is accessible and responsive.

Scope: IA diagram, updated left rail visual spec (compact + expanded states), workspace context component (compact pill + full switcher modal), prioritized route map, prototype flows for: workspace switch, moving between hosting modes, navigation to rollouts + cost detail, and keyboard quick-jump. Includes review notes and suggested rollout plan with A/B gating for telemetry collection.
acceptance_criteria: Left rail IA separates top-level global items from workspace-scoped items with clear affordance and label hierarchy.
Workspace context pill appears at top of left rail, shows current workspace name, type (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and a chevron to open quick switcher.
Quick switcher reachable via global shortcut (G W) and supports fuzzy search + keyboard selection; switching triggers client-side routing without full page reload.
Rollouts, Dashboards, and Cost views are visible within two clicks from the root of any workspace on desktop and one tap from search on mobile.
All new elements meet WCAG AA contrast and keyboard focus requirements; components tested in VoiceOver/NVDA.
Prototype validated with at least 3 engineering and 2 PM reviewers and one usability test with 5 participants (internal), feedback captured.
Telemetry hooks identified for click-through rates on workspace switcher, time-to-target-route, and fallback occurrences to global nav.
Migration notes provided for existing deep links: mapping table for old routes to new canonical routes.
Design sign-off and handoff package uploaded to Figma with tokens and component variants for left rail states.
QA checklist for responsive layout (>=320px) and keyboard navigation is produced and added to the ticket.
Engineering acceptance: a minimal spike and milestone plan included for runtime route guards and workspace context API usage.
decisions: Adopt two-tier left rail: top band = global (Account, Billing, Organization Admin); middle band = workspace context + primary workspace routes; bottom = utilities (feedback, help).
Workspace context should be persistent across routes and persist selected workspace id in client router state rather than relying solely on path prefix to reduce reloads.
Introduce a lightweight 'compact' left rail variant for small widths: icons only with longpress/hover tooltips and accessible labels.
Keyboard shortcut chosen: 'G W' to open Quick Switcher (consistent with other Redwood shortcuts), Esc closes modal and clears search box.
Cost views are promoted to a first-class section under 'Insights' for faster access; cost breakdown card persists in workspace home dashboard.
Rollouts get dedicated nav item when the workspace has >=1 active rollout; otherwise it is discoverable under 'Deployments' to reduce nav noise for small workspaces.

notes_for_engineering: Key constraints: preserve shareable URLs (canonical route required), avoid full page reloads on workspace switch, ensure server ACL checks fire after workspace switch. Provide a small API on client router to 'softSwitchWorkspace(workspaceId)' that updates state and triggers background permission refresh. Engineering to implement rollback region mapping for older deep links.
handoff_package: Figma file (see design_links) + tokens page and component variants. Also included a handoff checklist for CSS tokens, motion specs, and ARIA attributes.
open_questions: Should active-rollout badge be shown for all users or only workspace admins?
Do we allow pinning of routes within a workspace for power users? (proposal: allow, but limit to user-level preference storage).
How to surface multi-workspace alerts in the global header without adding noise to the left rail?
